title: Calling a Deer a Horse
text:
After the First Emperor of Qin died in 210 BC, the eunuch Zhao Gao helped put a weak younger son on the throne as the Second Emperor. Zhao Gao gradually made himself the real power at court, eliminating rivals, including the chancellor Li Si.

Sima Qian tells how, in 207 BC, Zhao Gao decided to find out which officials would dare oppose him. He brought a deer to court, presented it to the Second Emperor and said it was a horse.

The emperor laughed and said that the chancellor must be mistaken, calling a deer a horse. He asked the officials around him. Some kept silent. Some said it was a horse, to please Zhao Gao. Some said it was a deer. Afterward, Zhao Gao found ways to have those who had said "deer" punished under the law. From then on, Sima Qian says, every official at court feared him.

With no one willing to tell him the truth, the Second Emperor did not learn how serious the rebellions in the empire had become. Within months Zhao Gao forced him to commit suicide, and the Qin dynasty fell soon after. "Pointing at a deer and calling it a horse" became a Chinese idiom.
lesson: When people are punished for stating the obvious, everyone stops telling you the truth. Make it safe to say "that is a deer".
people: Zhao Gao, Qin Er Shi (the Second Emperor)
source: Sima Qian, Shiji (Records of the Grand Historian), chapter 6
